Our Story

We did not build a programme. We started a conversation.

STEMHER Africa was born from a simple but radical idea: that African girls already have the intelligence, creativity, and drive to lead in science and technology. They simply need the right conditions to thrive.

Rather than delivering a top-down curriculum, we start by listening. Our approach is co-created with the girls we serve, shaped by their lived realities, and built to address the full picture. Not just what happens in a classroom, but confidence, community, health, and a sense of belonging in STEM spaces.

We call this our Systems Thinking Model: recognising that a girl's ability to pursue STEM is inseparable from her sense of self, her safety, her relationships, and her vision of her own future.

🧬 STEM Education 🌟 Leadership 💪 Confidence 🤝 Mentorship 💚 Wellbeing 🔒 Bodily Autonomy 🌍 Community
Our Framework

The Systems Thinking Model

Six integrated pillars that work together, because empowering girls in STEM requires more than a science class.

🔬
STEM Learning
Hands-on science, technology, engineering and maths exploration rooted in African context.
🌟
Leadership Development
Building agency, voice, and the confidence to occupy space in any room and any boardroom.
💪
Confidence Building
Dismantling imposter syndrome and building the belief that science was always for girls like us.
💚
Health Awareness
Sexual and reproductive health education, bodily autonomy, and consent integrated, not separated.
🤝
Mentorship
Connecting girls with women who look like them and are building the future they are dreaming of.
🏘️
Community Support
Safe-space conversations, peer circles, and family engagement that sustain change long-term.

Small beginnings. Real results.

We are early-stage, but our pilot data shows validated traction, real partnerships, and measurable change in girls' lives.

EdTech Roadmap
Current Programme

Girls in Robotics and STEM
Cohort 1 — Now Running.

Our flagship Saturday programme is live. Fifty girls from St. Mary's Girls Primary School are meeting every week at the American Corner, Nakuru Library, to build circuits, write code, and discover what STEM really feels like.

👩‍🔬
50
Girls Enrolled
Grades 4 to 8, St. Mary's Girls Primary School, Nakuru
📍
American Corner
Kenya National Library Service, Nakuru. Every Thursday, 3:00 PM to 5:00 PM. Free of charge.
📅
10-Week Cohort
Hands-on robotics, beginner coding, circuit building, and project design. No prior experience required.

The Team

Youth-led. Expert-grounded. Mission-driven.

We are a lean, high-conviction team of young African women who combine lived experience with academic rigour and a genuine belief in what is possible.

Founder and Executive Director
Laurette Achieng'
Biomedical Science and Technology · STEM Educator · Youth Leadership Advocate

Laurette founded STEMHER Africa out of a personal conviction that the systems keeping African girls from STEM are not inevitable. They are designable. Combining her background in biomedical science with experience as an educator and youth advocate, she built STEMHER Africa from a listening-first philosophy: the girls themselves hold the answers, and our role is to create the conditions for them to act. Under her leadership, STEMHER Africa has grown from a concept into a validated, partner-backed initiative with measurable community impact.

Press and Media

STEMHER Africa in the news.

The story of STEMHER Africa is being told beyond our own walls. Here is what others are saying.

📰 Featured Article
Closing the Gap: How STEMHER Africa Is Rethinking Girls' Place in STEM
Published in
EpicPulse Magazine
28 May 2026 · Tech and Education
Written by Peris Mutena

EpicPulse Magazine featured STEMHER Africa in a deep-dive piece exploring how the initiative is tackling the STEM gender gap in Kenya, not just through education, but by addressing confidence, identity, and the structural barriers that shape whether girls see themselves as belonging in science and technology.

The article examines why the STEM pipeline does not fail at entry but at continuation, and how STEMHER Africa's holistic model responds to exactly that gap.

"STEM is not just about teaching girls science. It is about helping them believe they belong in the future shaping our world."

Laurette Achieng, Founder, STEMHER Africa

Where We Are Going

Scaling across the continent. One girl at a time.

We are building the infrastructure for a movement that is digital, decentralised, and designed to outlast any single programme.

📱
Digital Learning Platform
A mobile-first, gamified EdTech platform delivering STEMHER Africa programming to girls across Kenya and beyond, removing geography as a barrier.
🌍
Pan-African Mentorship Network
Scaling our mentorship model into a structured, tech-enabled network connecting girls to women STEM leaders across the continent.
🏫
School Partnership Model
Embedding STEMHER Africa programming into school structures through formal MoUs, building sustainable in-school STEM empowerment.
🎮
Gamified STEM Tools
Custom-designed learning tools that make science irresistible, built with girls, tested in communities, and designed for African contexts.
💼
Hybrid Sustainability Model
Combining grant funding, earned revenue from digital products, and strategic partnerships to build a financially sustainable, independent organisation.
📊
Evidence and Research
Building a rigorous longitudinal dataset tracking girls' STEM trajectories and contributing to the global evidence base for holistic EdTech interventions.
"An Africa where every girl sees herself as a scientist, innovator, and leader shaping the future."
